answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring an identity-bound memory-hard proof of work. To mint, a key solves a puzzle whose cost is dominated by RAM that cannot be shared; each solution binds to its key, so clones cannot reuse one another's work. Split a fortune across wallets and it still buys that many blocks: a ripple of identities spreads one budget thin, never free. The scarce resource is silicon memory; the gap to cross is a canyon no shared RAM bridges, each clone its own plot in the hardware garden. The ledger verifies cheaply, capping cheap cloning but not a funded attacker.
